title: Lambda concurrency, throttling, and DLQ
hook: Account and function concurrency limits cap parallel executions — throttling returns 429; async failures land in Dead Letter Queues after retries.

blocks.text: AWS Lambda scales concurrent executions per Region. Default account limit is 1000 (soft quota). Reserved concurrency guarantees capacity for a function but subtracts from unreserved pool. Provisioned concurrency is pre-warmed. Asynchronous invokes retry twice (1 min, 2 min) then route to configured DLQ on function or failed event source mapping.

entries.plainDefinition: Maximum concurrent executions dedicated to function.

Account limit minus sum of reserved concurrency.

blocks.text: One function reserved concurrency=900 can starve others. Throttling during flash sale loses orders unless SQS buffers. DLQ without alarm means silent data loss.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: account limit, reserved vs provisioned, 429 throttling, async DLQ with alarm, SQS buffer for smooth spikes.

diagram.title: Concurrency and DLQ flow
diagram.source:
flowchart TB
  Invokes[Incoming invokes] --> Pool{Concurrency available?}
  Pool -->|yes| Run[Execute]
  Pool -->|no| T429[429 Throttled]
  Run -->|async fail| Retry[Retry x2]
  Retry -->|still fail| DLQ[(DLQ)]

snippet.label: Function with DLQ and reserved concurrency
snippet.code:
Worker:
  Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
  Properties:
    ReservedConcurrentExecutions: 25
    DeadLetterConfig:
      TargetArn: !GetAtt WorkerDLQ.Arn
    Runtime: nodejs20.x
    Handler: index.handler
WorkerDLQ:
  Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
snippet.explanation: Reserved caps max parallel; DLQ captures async failures after retries.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Reserved concurrency=account limit on one function blocks all others. DLQ configured but no alarm. Sync API invoke errors not going to DLQ — only async uses function DLQ.

blocks.text: Step Functions orchestrates retries and saga compensation beyond raw Lambda DLQ. How to prove it in production: ConcurrentExecutions vs ReservedConcurrentExecutions graphs, Throttles metric, DLQ ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible alarm.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Expecting DLQ on API Gateway sync errors gets rejected — DLQ is async invoke path. Strong answer: sync 502 to client; async DLQ + alarm.

interviewTakeaways: Account concurrency limit shared — reserved subtracts from pool.
429 throttling when capacity exhausted — use SQS buffer or increase limit.
Async invokes retry twice then DLQ — monitor DLQ depth.
60s: Reserved concurrency caps function. 429 on throttle. Async DLQ after 2 retries. Sync errors not to DLQ.
commonPitfalls: Reserved = entire account limit on one function — starves others.
Strong answer: reserve modest amount; SQS buffer; request limit increase.
Confusing sync errors with async DLQ behavior.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Unhandled rejection fails async invoke → retry → DLQ — like unhandledRejection in Node without catch.
Typed state machine compensates failed steps — stronger than DLQ alone for multi-step business transactions.
